dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: "In but a night the jade is cut in twain, the spring rain pours forth time and again..."

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Wait, have I been reading this whole time? I should really start my sword practice...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Xingqiu? What are you up to?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Ah, what a coincidence, running into you here. I'm currently practicing my swordsmanship.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: ...Well, perhaps it's more correct to say that I'm practicing my penmanship.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Yes. Quite the novelty, no?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: See these fallen leaves? They're my calligraphic copybook. Some are sliced down the middle, others cut along the veins, or chopped into pieces, and each represents one of three different calligraphic scripts.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Scripts... you say?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Hahaha, yup, they're all forms of calligraphy, each with its own unique features. Some are neat and orderly, and others are more free-form and expressive...

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: I must say that I have enjoyed my practice, though I can't say the same for the bamboo around me...

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Ah, this time, I truly did become the autumn storm that sweeps through the forest.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Was the phrase you were reading before some kind of secret mantra?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: A secret mantra? Oh, no, no. I was just reading the annotations in this book, "Chronicle of Cleansing Ink."

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: This book is quite marvelous indeed, and was written by a calligraphy master named Xifan. It is said that he shifted from calligraphy to swordsmanship, and afterwards attained mastery of both.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: After that, he did not hoard what he had gained, writing his swordsmanship down on a stone tablet and naming it the "Chronicle of Cleansing Ink," making it free for all who follow the noble path of chivalry to come and see it.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: This particular book is a rare "original annotated copy" with contents all transcribed from the original stone tablet. My brother really treasures this one.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: My brother is usually a giving and generous soul, but he loves books as much as his own life. Trying to borrow even one from him is like pulling teeth.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: I'll be honest, he scared me half to death when he handed me this copy a few days back, urging me to "go practice my calligraphy."

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: I had thought that I was about to be disowned on account of my terrible penmanship, and he was giving me the book as a farewell gift after having heard the news in advance.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: You should've seen the two of us, weeping and wailing, our hands clutching the book, refusing to let go...

choices.text: I suspect he was just reluctant to leave the book in your hands...

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Hahaha, oh, come on, you! You just had to come right out and say it, didn't you? Well, I thought the scene was pretty funny. In fact, I'd like to include it in my novel.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: And if I were to include your follow-up remark as well, I'm sure that would add some extra flavor...

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Oh my, we talked so much I lost track of time again! It's getting late, so I must hurry home.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: #I'll see you around, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: And that you just really didn't want to practice, huh...
Your pen is quite the dangerous thing, then...

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Hahaha. Don't worry, I've already finished practice, and my pen's safely back in its box.
